text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

After failing to gain the backing of ANI's institutional shareholders for his push to change the board over deals relating to German environmental engineering group Holter, former steel tube baron Ross Palmer, who was dumped from the ANI board at the compny's annual meeting last month, has sold his stake in the engineering giant for a loss of A$24 million. Page 1.

In a last-minute attempt to head off tough trade sanctions before the arrival in Australia of US President Bill Clinton, Federal Cabinet discussed a deal yesterday which would see Australia agree to isolate car upholstery maker Howe Leather from the Goverment's import credit scheme, while Washington would, in return, drop its World Trade Organisation challenge to Howe Leather and promise not to start any action against other parts of Australia's car and textile industry plans. Page 1.

The Wool Council of Australia yesterday accused the Federal Government of being too scared to raise difficult issues with US President Bill Clinton when he visits Australia. Council president Rod Thirkell-Johnston urged the Coalition to raise the issue of US quotas and tariffs on imports of wool products with Clinton, but feared the meeting would become a back-slapping, "all-the-way-with-LBJ" exercise. Page 4.

After a proposal giving authority for the issue of convertible preference shares was forced to a poll at Boral Ltd's annual general meeting in Sydney yesterday, the move ultimately won approval with 89.1 per cent of the vote. Chairman Peter Cottrell alsotold shareholders that operating profit for the first four months of the financial year was 20 per cent behind last year, but was in line with budget. Page 21.

Bringing an end to its 70 percent rise over the past few months, investors yesterday slashed more than A$1 billion off the market capitalisation of C-C Amatil Ltd following the announcement that the company had failed to meet budget in the last three quaters and that its 1996 profits were unlikely to better 1995's result of A$138.6 million. Page 21.

Austrim Ltd chairman Alan Jackson yesterday defended the merit of conglomerates, telling the company's annual general meeting that Austrim could make another acquisition of up to A$70 million to add to its growing

collection of businesses. Jackson said the management task in a conglomerate was not impossible and many analysts, who have been downgrading such companies, simply have difficulty in understanding 10 or 12 or 15 businesses. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Due to a sustained increase in the copper price, which, buoyed by 10 weeks of decline in inventories on the London Metal Exchange, crashed through the crucial US$1 a pound barrier on Friday, international copper giants RTZ-CRA and BHP - the world's largest publicly owned copper producer - have been fundamentally re-rated by Australian investors. Page 19.

News of an improvement in the chronically weak building materials business Boral Ltd was overshadowed at the group's annual meeting in Sydney yesterday as both the chairman Peter Cottrell and managing director Tony Berg were grilled over plans for an issue of converting preference shares. Page 19.

Despite quitting his five per cent stake in heavy engineering group Australian National Industries yesterday for A$50.8 million and suffering a loss of up to A$25 million in the process, disgruntled former ANI director Ross Palmer has warned the group ha snot heard the last of him and he said he still held hopes for the removal of Peter Joseph and Howard Stack from the ANI board. Page 19.

Responding to criticism by the Australian Payments System Council over the failure of the financial sector to speed up cheque processing, Australian Payments Clearing Association chief executive officer Peter Smith said yesterday consumers would have to wait at least another year to gain the benefits of faster cheque clearance. Page 19.

Coles Myer Ltd board hopeful Peter Willcocks said yesterday he believes he can raise a motion at today's annual meeting in Sydney challenging the controversial method of electing directors in the retail group, however, he conceded that the motion might be ruled out of order by chairman Nobby Clark. Page 21.

A special Australian National Audit Office audit of Australian Taxation Office debt collection methods - tabled in Parliament yesterday - has found improved collection of outstanding tax payments will save Federal Treasury at least A$142 million annually. The report identified 29 measures to tighten the ATO's debt collection techniques. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Building supplies and energy group Boral joined a long list of Australian companies in predicting tough trading conditions for the rest of this year and consequent pressure on profits due to the slow economy and fierce competition at its annual general meeting yesterday. Page 27.

Former Australian National Industries director and dissident shareholder Ross Palmer's Tube Securities yesterday sold a A$50 million, 4.9 percent stake in engineering group ANI at A$1.27-a-share, later citing disappointment with the board and institutionl shareholders for failing to enforce proper
corporate governance. Page 27.

In a statement accompanying Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting's submission to the Federal Government's inquiry into cross-media rules, PBL managing director James Packer called for an immediate dismantling of the "obsolete" cross-media rules and tougher controls on foreign ownership to ensure Australian cultural interests are protected. Page 27.

Coca Cola Amatil shares fell A$2.04, or 13 percent, yesterday to close at A$15.50, wiping A$1.1 billion off the group's market capitalisation and ending 16 months of virtually constant rises, as angry investors responded to the soft drinks group's warning that its profit for the December year would be little changed from last year's. Page 27.

Speaking in Sydney yesterday, Sir Colin Marshall, British Airways chairman and a Qantas Airways non-executive director, said global jet fuel prices, which have jumped more then 20 percent this year, are putting serious pressure on Qantas's A$330 million cost-cutting programme for the 1997 financial year. Page 29.

John Filmer, director of Optus' corporate and government division, says Optus Communications will charge businesses and Government a flat rate for its Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) data transmission when the service comes onstream next year and claimsthe new technology can save corporate Australia A$100 million a year. Page 29.
THE AGE

While conceding yesterday that the construction industry was on the verge of a synchronised upturn, Boral managing director Tony Berg became the latest chief of a leading Australian company to predict tough conditions and stagnant profits because of the slow economy and fierce competition. Page C1.

More than A$1.1 billion was stripped from the market value of Coca-Cola Amatil yesterday on the back of news last week that CCA's trading results over the past three months had not met budget and that its 1996 net profit would show little
change over 1995. Many analysts complained that CCA had misled them over its outlook during two recent tours of the bottler's overseas operations. Page C1.

Companies with tenements in the sparsely explored Gawler region in South Australia received a lift in their share prices yesterday, following the announcement by gold explorer Helix Resources NL that it had struck gold at its Tunkilla prospect in the sand covered Gawler Craton. Page C1.

Former Australian National Industries ANIK.AX director Ross Palmer yesterday sold almost all his A$50 million stake in the engineering group, claiming he was disappointed with the board and institutional shareholders for failing to enforce proper corporate governnce. Palmer's Tube Securities sold 38.68 million shares at A$1.27 each. Page C3.

National Australia Bank announced yesterday it would launch a full pilot of stored-value cards early next year, heading up what is expected to be a rush of further trials following news that MasterCard International has sealed a A$150 million deal to buy majority stake in the British smart cards group Mondex International. Page C3.

Klaus Albrecht, the managing director of Deutsche Bank's Australian arm, yesterday ruled out a local takeover target for the bank, saying that the bank "did not feel comfortable" entering retail banking in an environment as competitive as Australia's. The announcement ended speculation that Deutsche was preparing a bid for ANZ Bank after the Wallis inquiry reports early next year. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
